New Loan FacilityandOperational Update
Kropz Plc (AIM: KRPZ), an emerging African phosphate producer and developer, announces that Kropz Elandsfontein (Pty) Ltd ("
Elandsfontein
")
and Ubunto-Botho Investments (Pty) Ltd
("
UBI
")
(together the "
Parties
") have agreed to a ZAR 200 million (approximately US$ 12.3 million) (the "
Loan
"), which constitutes a related party transaction.
Operational Update
The Elandsfontein mine continues to progress through its production ramp-up phase. As previously announced, record monthly production was achieved in March with over 40,000 tonnes of production. However, mining operations continue to be materially affected by variability in the ore body, including the nature and volume of slimes material, hard bank and pink ore encountered within the deposit. These conditions have resulted in slower mining rates and lower concentrate output in the quarter ended 30 June 2026. Production was also disrupted in the quarter due to availability of the mining contractor, which interrupted ore flow to the processing plant and constrained the operational flexibility required to sustain more stable production levels.
Geopolitical tensions have created additional commercial headwinds with higher energy and consumable costs, and an increase in freight rates.
Elandsfontein produced 95 956 tonnes of phosphate concentrate in quarter ended 30 June 2026 (115,686: quarter to 31 March 2026) representing a 17% decrease compared quarter to quarter. Sales for the period totalled 183,714 tonnes, and stock at the quarter end was higher than anticipated being approximately 94,000 tonnes.
The operational issues, combined with the market factors described above, has given rise to a further working capital funding requirement. Consequently, the Company has entered into the Loan with UBI to support the group.
The Loan will be used by Elandsfontein to fund its cashflow and operational expenditure needs.
The Loan
Elandsfontein and UBI have agreed terms for a loan facility of ZAR 200 million (approximately US$ 12.3 million). Interest is payable on the Loan at the South African prime overdraft interest rate plus 6%, nominal per annum and compounded monthly. The Loan is repayable on the earlier of a date as agreed between the Parties or on demand from UBI, on no less than 15 business days' notice. There is no fixed term.
As announced on 21 May 2025 and 28 May 2025, Kropz SA (Pty) Ltd has issued a Guarantee, Security Cession and Pledge in favour of the ARC Fund (
ARC
), and Kropz Plc has issued a Limited Indemnity, Security Cession and Pledge in favour of ARC for all current and future loan facilities made to Elandsfontein, which are applicable to the Loan.These agreements will be extended by the parties in favour of UBI as the first ranking priority (through an Omnibus agreement), and ARC and the second ranking priority issued by Kropz SA (Pty) Ltd for all current and future loan facilities of Kropz Elandsfontein.
The Company will update the market on drawdown of the Loan in due course.
Related Party Transaction
UBI is the indirect controlling shareholder of ARC, and consequently the Loan and the Omnibus agreement are related party transactions pursuant to Rule 13 of the AIM Rules for Companies. Gerrit Duminy, a director of the Company, is the representative of ARC. Accordingly, Gerrit Duminy has not been involved in the approval of the Loan by the Company's board. The directors of the Company, who are considered independent for the purposes of the Loan, having consulted with the Company's nominated adviser, consider the terms of the Loan to be fair and reasonable insofar as the Company's shareholders are concerned.

company_30s.what_they_do: Kropz Limited is a mining exploration and development company focused on the Hinda project in the Republic of Congo. The project is a copper‑cobalt prospect that the company is working to bring into production, with plans to build a mine and associated processing facilities once feasibility is proven.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The Congo region contains some of the world’s largest copper and cobalt deposits, which are critical to the global shift toward electric vehicles and renewable energy. If Kropz can successfully develop Hinda, it would tap into a high‑growth commodity market and position itself as a key supplier to major mining and technology firms.
company_30s.current_state: Kropz is still in the exploration and financing phase, with no revenue yet. The company is burning cash to fund drilling, feasibility studies and regulatory approvals. It is trading near the lower end of its 52‑week range, reflecting a market that has largely discounted its prospects.

rns_narrative: The company has been busy shuffling its financing structure, drawing down on a bridge loan, then securing a new loan facility and announcing a WRAP retail offer. These moves suggest a tight liquidity position but also a willingness to raise capital to keep the project alive.

Corporate governance has seen changes as well: a new nominated adviser was appointed and the company received ECA approval, signalling progress toward meeting regulatory requirements for a public listing in the UK.

Operational updates have been sparse, with the latest news focusing on loan terms and a brief trading update. There is no concrete evidence yet that the Hinda project has moved beyond the feasibility stage.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Quiet with sporadic optimism about the Hinda project
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: A handful of traders are bullish, pointing to the potential of the Hinda project and the possibility that a successful feasibility study could unlock a new source of copper and cobalt.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bears cite the repeated drawdown of bridge loans, the lack of revenue, and the high cash burn as red flags that the company may struggle to stay afloat without additional funding.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The tone has moved from cautious to uncertain: initial excitement about the project has been dampened by the financial strain, but a few hopeful voices remain.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends is flat – any news or announcement is likely to produce a sizeable surprise move.

near_term_catalysts: Closing of the new loan facility or successful completion of the WRAP retail offer – a clear injection of cash.
Release of a positive feasibility study for Hinda, confirming viable production economics.
Approval of any required environmental or mining permits that would allow the company to move from exploration to development.
A significant commodity price move in copper or cobalt that would improve the project’s economics.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a volume spike and a breakout above the current resistance level, coupled with a funding announcement or a positive operational update. A sustained rally on higher volume would confirm a mean‑reversion thesis.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock is in the early stages of a crash‑recovery cycle. The APEX score suggests compression, but the market has not yet reacted to any catalyst. A bounce is expected once the company secures funding or shows a concrete operational win.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: The stock is deeply discounted – a 70‑95% plunge from its pre‑crash level. If the company clears its financing hurdle or delivers a positive feasibility, the price could rebound to roughly 50% of its pre‑crash level, delivering a 200% gain from the current price. Historical red‑color signals show similar outsized rebounds, and the lack of public interest keeps the floor low.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: Liquidity remains a major risk. If the new loan fails to close or the WRAP offer is withdrawn, the company could run out of cash and face delisting or forced sale of assets. The absence of any revenue stream means the upside is contingent on a single project moving forward.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential upside is at least twice the current price, while downside is limited to the present level if the market stays flat. The asymmetry is roughly 3:1 – a small loss versus a sizeable win.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter on a breakout above the current resistance with a 5‑10% position size relative to total capital. Place a stop 10% below the entry to protect against a sudden reversal. Target 50% of the pre‑crash level as the primary profit point, with a secondary target at the original peak.
playbook.if_watching: Hold until a funding announcement or a positive feasibility report is released, and the volume spikes by at least 20% above the 20‑day average. Only then consider entering with the same risk parameters as above.
playbook.if_passing: If the company fails to secure the new loan or the WRAP offer is cancelled, or if there is a clear indication of delisting, exit the position immediately. The absence of any realistic funding path would make the upside improbable.

ai_insights.bottom_line: Kropz is a deep‑crashed mining play that could rebound dramatically if it secures fresh funding or a positive feasibility report, offering a highly asymmetric upside with limited downside.
